story: Man dies charging iPhone while in the bath
text: TL;DR: spend the $19 to buy a real, big brand USB charger because they have more to lose than grey market no brand. Tragic. Probably cheap USB without mains isolation or maybe enough water dripped down length of cable and socket to create a circuit, because USB is supposed to be 5V DC. Watch these USB charger teardown horror-shows to further understand why it's rational to pay for proper, authentic CE+UL, high-low isolation and quality components (ie insulated tape in transformers): [VIDEO] [LINK] [LINK] [LINK] [LINK] [LINK]

text: Finally a possible explanation [1] as to why Apple chargers (USB and laptop) give you tingles when touching the metal casing of the device they're plugged into. story: Searching for USB Power Supplies That Won't Explode
text: Sometimes even a well designed and assembled power supply can be dangerous because of defective components. Big Clive on Youtube does many teardowns of cheap electronics, and here's one of a USB power supply that's dangerous because of internal damage to the transformer: [VIDEO] Because this is an intermittent fault it's possible that non-destructive testing would not find it.

story: California appeals court finds Amazon responsible for 3rd party sellers products
text: It stands to reason that selling arbitrary offshore products without liability insurance will come to an end. Almost every offshore brand and reseller has a throwaway name so they can just fold up and start over should anything happen. No more cheap/counterfeit USB deathdapters [VIDEO] Also, I think electrical, li-ion, and RF products will have to prove their safety and compliance certification paperwork.
